newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates drop due to maturities.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates drop due to maturities.

text.p: *Central Bank overnight lending unchanged at 15 pct
Philippine interbank call loan rates dropped for the third straight day on Thursday, helped by inflows from maturing Treasury bills, traders said.
The average rate slipped to 11.0625 percent from 11.50, with done rates ranging from 11.03125 to 11.3125 percent.
Volume narrowed to 16.174 billion from 19.770 billion pesos. Of 45 participating financial institutions, 26 were lenders.
Traders estimate a net of 2.3 billion pesos were added to the system from maturing Treasury bills.
Despite the lower interest rates, banks still anticipate tightness due to the high spending during the Christmas season.
"Right now, everyone's concern is covering for the year-end," said a foreign bank dealer.
Dealers said this prompted more demand for 60-day money so banks would have enough money to tide them over the end of 1996.
At the secondary market trading of T-bills, there were more buyers since banks had more pesos to invest in government securities, dealers said.
The three-month bills were quoted a bid rate of 11.70 to 11.90 percent; the six months at 12.375 to 12.60; and the one year at 12.725 to 13.0.
